brief: The canvas displays a dense, sepia-toned sheet of newsprint covered in thousands of tiny, redundant textual fragments. These scraps appear as marginalia, crossed-out words, and overlapping failures of print, rendered in the visible state of wet ink. The colors are limited to faded black and deep brown against the fibrous, cream-colored background. Over time, the wet ink continuously and unpredictably bleeds, blooms, and smears across the surface, causing existing text to dissolve into abstract, spreading patches of color. This process of textual decay and organic structural failure happens constantly and automatically, making the surface appear perpetually unstable.

statement: This sketch simulates the deteriorating surface of aged newsprint, where thousands of textual fragments appear as marginalia and crossed-out words. The work depicts a continuous process of decay through wet ink bleeding and spreading across the paper. Text fragments slowly move and fade, while organic ink blobs bloom and smear unpredictably across the canvas. The sepia-toned palette evokes the aged appearance of newspaper, with faded black text on cream-colored background. The constant motion and spontaneous dissolution of elements create an impression of perpetual instability and textual failure, capturing the essence of paper that has been subjected to time, moisture, and physical stress.
